title: The 34-year wait
topic: Big falls take time to recover

steps.title: From 1989 to 2024
steps.body: Japan's main stock index reached a peak at the end of 1989. The index measures the value of Japan's biggest companies. By 2009, it had fallen by about 80%. It went above the old peak only in 2024, 34 years later. A fall from a previous high is called a [[drawdown]]. Having much of your money in one place is called [[concentration-risk]]. The numbers are rounded.

stat.label: for Japan's market to beat its 1989 high

steps.prompt: After a loss, the price must rise more than it fell. Find the loss that needs a rise of 400%.

output.label: Rise needed to get back to the start

goal.hint: Look at how much Japan's index fell by 2009.

steps.prompt: Look at the chart. What happened to money invested at the peak in 1989?
options: It fell by about 80% and took 34 years to get back
It grew a little every year
It fell, and then recovered within two years
steps.explanation: The index fell from 100 in 1989 to about 20 in 2009. It went back above 100 only in 2024. A deep [[drawdown]] can last longer than a working life.

chart.caption: Japan's main stock index. The value in 1989 is set to 100. The numbers are rounded.

steps.prompt: An investment loses 50%. After that, it grows by 7% each year. How many years until it is back at the start?
steps.reveal: About 10 years. After a 50% loss, the investment must grow by 100%. At 7% a year, money doubles in about 10 years. If you need the money sooner, it may not recover in time.

steps.prompt: True or false: after a 50% fall, a 50% rise brings you back to the start.
steps.explanation: False. €100 falls to €50. A 50% rise on €50 is €25, so you have €75. To get back to €100, you need a rise of 100%. This is how a [[drawdown]] works.

steps.title: Your biggest investment
steps.body: Your investment account holds **{depotTotal}**. Your biggest single investment is **{largestPositionShare}** of it. If that one investment falls, your whole account falls with it. That is [[concentration-risk]].

stat.label: of your account sits in one investment

steps.prompt: Imagine your biggest investment falls 60% and everything else stays the same. Try other shares.

goal.hint: Move the slider to see the result change.

steps.note: The slider starts at your real share. This is an example, not a forecast.

scenes.title: 34 years
scenes.desc: Japan's stock market fell by about 80% and needed 34 years to recover. How long your money can wait is your [[time-horizon]]. The numbers are rounded.
